To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LDCVs in mammalian neurons contain a large number of high MW transmitters and that their cargo is selectively stored in a subset of vesicles that undergoes a process of condensation and reduction in size.

LDCVs in the central nervous system are heterogeneous in terms of cargo and size, but homogeneous in their molecular composition, and that the release of their content is a process of partial exocytosis.
LDCVs in the central terminals of rat dorsal root ganglia neurons are smaller than those in cell bodies and that they contain the same cargo.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms of synthesis, storage and release of multiple high MW neurotransmitters and with the possible existence of selective sorting and/or differential fusion of LDCVs containing different cargoes.
the mechanisms of synthesis, storage and release of multiple high MW neurotransmitters in LDCV of different types of neurons.
the molecular composition and functional properties of LDCVs and with the mechanisms of their formation and release.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although there is still much to learn about the molecular mechanisms underlying the synthesis and storage in LDCVs of different types of high MW transmitters, there is no evidence for the existence of LDCVs that contain only one type of transmitter or that are differentially targeted to specific axonal branches.

, although the field is still in its infancy, the available evidence suggests that LDCVs of neurons are not only heterogeneous in size, but also that they may be heterogeneous in their molecular content and in the way in which they interact with axolemma.

LDCVs are not a homogeneous population of vesicles but rather a heterogeneous one, and that their composition and mode of release may vary depending on their site of localization in a given neuron and on the type of neurotransmitter stored therein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

LDCVs are a highly heterogeneous population of vesicles, each type containing a specific cargo and a unique combination of integral proteins, and that they are filled and released at different sites along neuronal processes.
the LDCVs of different types of neurons are not only morphologically and functionally heterogeneous, but they are also heterogeneous in terms of their protein composition.
the LDCV is a dynamic structure, which can undergo multiple cycles of filling, transport and release, with the possibility of being recycled back to the cell body.
The main takeaway from our work is that

LDCVs in the spinal cord terminals are smaller than those at cell body and, in particular, that the LDCVs in CGRP-immunoreactive terminals of the dorsal horn are smaller than those in terminals of the superficial dorsal horn.
the size of Ldcvs is a reliable parameter to evaluate the degree of maturation of the secretory organelles.
